blurb: A lambda parameter may be a pattern only when it is a record pattern that cannot fail, as in `(Item { qty, .. }) => qty`. A lambda is given a value and has no `else`, so a pattern that can miss, such as `Some(n)`, a list, a literal or a range, has no way to say what happens then. Take a name and `match` on it in the body.
example:
xs.map((Some(n)) => n)               // ✗ a lambda has no `else` for `None`

xs.map((o) => match o {              // ✓ the `match` covers both
    Some(n) => n
    None => 0
})
summary: A lambda parameter is a pattern other than a record pattern; only an irrefutable record pattern may stand in for a name.
